title: Fusarium wilt disease in outdoor tomatoes

Header: Fusarium wilt disease in outdoor tomatoes
Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici Mnyauko Fusarii in Swahili

Prevention: Use non-infected clean seeds from healthy tomatoes, or certified clean seeds from authorized dealer.
Do not make compost and mulch from plants from infected fields.
Avoid injuring plants when working in the field.
Sterilize tools and shoes in case fields are in a
Fusarium -infected area (e.g. with bleach, which is
Wear gloves or wash hands with plenty water afterwards, because bleach is toxic.
Do not use stakes from infected fields to stake tomato plants in disease-free areas
Fusarium wilt is detected in a part of your field, go to this area last after managing healthy plants.
Avoid furrow and flood irrigation because water can move this disease (if using furrow irrigation ensure that water flows from new to old fields).
Long crop rotations of 5-7 years would be needed to reduce the disease in the soil.
Monitoring: Fusarium wilt, also called basal rot, is a fungal disease of tomatoes.
Concentrate searching for symptoms on mature plants after flowering and at the beginning of fruit set, but seedlings can also be affected.
Search for yellowing and wilting of individual branches and leaves, but rarely entire plants.
The disease starts with the lower, older leaves.
The disease is often found on one side of a branch or plant.
But later it spreads and can kill the plant.
If you these symptoms, cut into the stem at the base of the plant to reveal a dark- brown to red discoloration inside the stem due to the disease.
When a single infected plant is found then actions should be considered.
Direct Control: It is easier to prevent this disease than to control it.
Remove and destroy entire diseased plant.
Carry materials away from the field in a closed container such as a plastic bag to prevent the spread of the disease.
Restrictions: There is no effective direct chemical control measure available
